headline: UK Museums Stay Free for All Visitors After Government Review
meta_description: Britain's 14 national museums, including the British Museum and National Gallery, will remain free to all visitors after the government rejected a proposal to…

body:
Britain's government has reaffirmed its commitment to keeping the country's 14 national museums free for all visitors, rejecting a proposal that would have charged international tourists while maintaining free admission for citizens and residents. The decision, announced after months of consultations with the tourism sector, local communities, and cultural institutions, preserves a landmark policy established by Tony Blair's Labour government in 2001. Museums affected by the decision include the National Gallery, the British Museum, and the Natural History Museum—institutions that together welcome tens of millions of visitors annually.

The debate arose following an independent review published in December by former Labour minister Margaret Hodge, who noted that countries like New Zealand and Singapore successfully charge overseas visitors while keeping museums free for their own citizens. However, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport ultimately concluded that such a charging model would discourage domestic visitors and create uneven impacts across the sector. "The government believes that charging overseas visitors could deter domestic visitors," the department stated, signalling that cultural accessibility trumped potential revenue concerns.

London Mayor Sadiq Khan welcomed the decision as a victory for inclusivity. "By keeping these important venues open to all, we will continue to educate and entertain generations to come and show why we are the culture capital of the world," Khan said. The ruling ensures that whether visitors arrive from across Britain or across the globe, these world-class institutions remain welcoming spaces dedicated to learning, wonder, and shared human experience.
